description: baseline

Replace the no-op baseline in submissions/arena/ with the futurebiohackers airbench96-style recipe as published (A1a): frozen 2x2 patch-whitening stem, 3-conv groups at widths 128/384/576, SGD-Nesterov lr 9 with BN biases at 64x LR, label smoothing 0.3, lookahead-EMA, alternating flip + translate 2, 8.5 epochs, bs 1024, fp16 + channels_last, GPU-resident uint8 data with GPU-side augmentation. In build, run torch.compile max-autotune and warm it up on synthetic inputs for both train and eval shapes, including eval batch sizes 1..1024 or dynamic, and the cuDNN/CUDA init. E000 showed lazy init landing in the first timed trial. Log the per-trial prepare and train split.
Rerun the A1a reproduction byte-identical, with no code change, to measure run-to-run time and accuracy noise. Record the per-seed accuracy std and the per-trial prepare/train times from both runs.
On top of A1a, replace every GELU activation with SiLU (same compile and epochs). If the reference already uses ReLU or SiLU, test GELU->ReLU on whichever activation it does use.

On top of A1a, compute the patch-whitening eigendecomposition on the first 1500 training images instead of 5000, and do normalization in fp16 on the GPU in one fused pass. Instrument prepare time separately.
On top of A1a, widen the last group from 576 to 768 channels and cut epochs from 8.5 to 7.5. Recompile and warm up the new shapes in build.

On top of A1a, train at 24 px for the first ~40% of epochs, 28 px for the next ~30% and 32 px for the rest, with random-resized crops on the GPU. Add +0.5 epochs (9.0 total). Compile and warm up all three shapes in build so no recompile happens in timed code. The final EMA/eval runs at 32 px.

Control run for H1.4.1, and the epoch-slope point for H1. Start from A1a (E001 tip) and change only the epoch count, from 8.5 to 8.0. Scale the LR and lookahead/EMA schedule to the new total step count the same way the recipe already does. Leave everything else byte-identical. Log the per-seed accuracies.

Take the 8.0-epoch recipe from the control idea and add light brightness/contrast jitter in the existing GPU-side augmentation. Per image, multiply by a contrast factor drawn uniformly from [0.85, 1.15] around the per-image mean, then add a brightness offset drawn uniformly from [-0.1, 0.1] (in normalized units), before the flip/translate step. Apply it to training batches only and keep it a single fused elementwise op. Change nothing else.

On the 8.0-epoch recipe, lower label smoothing from 0.3 to 0.2. Change nothing else. This tests whether the reference hyperparameters, which were tuned at 8.5 epochs, leave accuracy on the table at shorter schedules. Shorter training usually wants less regularization.

On top of A1a, raise the batch size from 1024 to 2000 at equal epochs. Scale lr, wd and EMA/lookahead intervals by the kilostep rule: keep lr*wd per example, and scale the step-based schedule by the step count. Warm up the new shapes in build.

Start from A1a. Make the optimizer fused: torch.optim.SGD(fused=True) if PyTorch 2.4 accepts it for this param-group setup, otherwise foreach=True. Wrap the optimizer step plus the lookahead/EMA update in a single torch.compile'd function and warm it up in build on synthetic gradients. Keep the epochs (8.5) and all hyperparameters unchanged. This also tests the E004 power-cap lesson, which predicts little gain from cutting overhead alone.

Start from A1a (8.5 epochs). From the start of epoch 3, for each batch of 1024: (1) run a no-grad forward through the compiled net in train mode, with BN running-stat updates disabled, and get per-example losses; (2) keep the 614 highest-loss examples (a fixed size, so the shapes stay static); (3) run the normal forward+backward and optimizer step on those 614 only. Compile and warm up the 614-shape train step in build. Keep the LR schedule tied to the step count, which does not change.

Start from A1a (E001 tip) and add progressive resizing with a long full-res tail. Total 9.0 epochs (LR/EMA/lookahead schedules rescaled to the step count as the recipe already does). Train at 26 px for steps 0-30%, 28 px for 30-60% and 32 px for the last 40%. Low-res batches are made by applying the existing flip + translate-2 at 32 px, then F.interpolate(mode='bilinear', antialias=True) to 26/28 px. No random-resized crop. The final group pool must still end at 3x3 (26->25->12->6->3, 28->27->13->6->3). In build, compile and warm up all 3 train shapes plus eval at 32 px, so nothing recompiles in timed code. Instrumentation only: log a hash of the first batch's augmentation parameters per trial.

Take E006's schedule unchanged: 9.0 epochs, epochs 0-3 low-res, 4-6 at 28 px, 7-8 at 32 px. Make exactly two changes, which together are the H2.5 confound removal: (a) the first phase uses 26 px instead of 24 px, and (b) replace random-resized crop with flip + translate-2 at 32 px followed by an antialiased bilinear downsample to the phase resolution. Warm up all shapes in build.

On the 8.0-epoch recipe (the E007 control, 0.7502 / 6.80 s), change only the LR schedule's end point: decay linearly to 0 at the last step instead of to 0.07x the peak. Keep warmup, peak LR, the BN-bias multiplier and the lookahead/EMA schedule unchanged. Being zero-cost, the resulting accuracy lever can stack onto any progressive-resizing recipe.

Take the H2.1.2 recipe (9.0 epochs; 26 px for 0-30%, 28 px for 30-60%, 32 px for the last 40%). Change only how low-res batches are made. Crop mode: after flip + translate-2 at 32 px, take a random 26x26 or 28x28 crop (independent offset per image, done via unfold/gather or a batched index on the GPU), with no rescaling, so object scale matches the test images. Do not use the antialiased downsample. Keep the shapes identical so the compiled graphs are reused.

On A1a (8.5 epochs, everything else unchanged), narrow group 2 from 384 to 320 channels, which also shrinks group 3's first conv input. Recompile and warm up in build. Group 2 at 15x15 carries ~50% of conv FLOPs by a rough count. 384->320 cuts total conv FLOPs by about 15%. The exchange rate to beat is the epoch-cut rate, 0.08 pp per 1% of time (E007).

On E006's code (commit ed8dc49), add only a FixRes-style BN re-estimation at the end of train. After the final EMA/lookahead weights are set, reset the BN running stats and run a forward-only pass in train mode (momentum=None, cumulative average) at 32 px over ~5000 augmented training images (5 batches of 1024, flip + translate only), under no_grad. Warm up this shape in build (it is the existing 32 px train shape).

On A1a (8.5 epochs), switch the 3x3 conv filters of the three groups to Muon: lr ~0.24, momentum 0.6, Nesterov, 3 Newton-Schulz steps in bf16, filters reshaped to [out, in*9]. Keep SGD-Nesterov with the existing hyperparameters for BN params, biases and the head. Keep the LR schedule shape and the lookahead/EMA. Warm up the compiled NS step in build. This is an explore run on the one optimization-efficiency lever not yet tried; E008 suggests the short schedule is under-fitting.

Start from the E019 Muon recipe (commit 45b511c): Muon on the 9 group 3x3 convs, lr 0.24, momentum 0.6, Nesterov, 3 NS steps in bf16; SGD for BN/biases/head; lookahead-EMA. Change only the epoch count, from 8.5 to 7.0. Rescale the LR, lookahead and EMA schedules to the new total step count, the same way the recipe already does (as in E007). Leave the Muon step code eager and unchanged so the run measures the Muon accuracy-vs-epochs slope with no confound. Log per-seed accuracies.

Port the two-stage 24->32 px progressive schedule to the E019 Muon recipe. 8.0 total epochs: epochs 0-3 at 24 px, epochs 4-7 at 32 px, no 28 px phase. Use the E006 operator: flip + translate-2 at 32 px, then F.interpolate(bilinear, antialias=True) to 24 px, with AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) as the final pool. Rescale the LR/EMA/lookahead schedules to the step count. Keep the Muon step eager as in E019. In build, compile and warm up both train shapes and the 32 px eval, so nothing recompiles in timed code.

On E019's Muon recipe at 8.5 epochs, raise the batch size from 1024 to 2000. Scale the SGD param groups (BN/bias/head) by the same kilostep rule as E010, and scale the EMA/lookahead schedule by the step count. Keep Muon lr 0.24 and momentum 0.6, which are airbench94_muon's own settings at bs 2000. Warm up the new shapes in build. This tests whether Muon removes the large-batch penalty SGD showed (E010: -0.81 pp) while halving the per-step Muon overhead.

On E019's Muon recipe (8.5 epochs), replace every exact GELU with nn.GELU(approximate='tanh'). Change nothing else, and recompile/warm up in build. Running this on the Muon base means the expected ~1% saving can be kept even with perturbation noise, since that base has 1.3 pp of margin.

Start from the E021 tip (commit bf93586: Muon + 4@24 + 4@32 px, 8.0 epochs). Change only how the Muon update runs. Wrap the whole update in a single function: momentum/Nesterov, bf16 3-step Newton-Schulz batched over same-shape filters (conv2/conv3 of each group stacked into one bmm), scale, and the weight update. Compile it with torch.compile(mode='max-autotune-no-cudagraphs'), and pass the LR as a 0-d GPU tensor so the schedule never recompiles. Warm it up in build on synthetic gradients for every filter shape. Keep the math, hyperparameters, schedule and data pipeline unchanged. Log per-trial train time.

On the E021 tip, change only the resolution split: 5 epochs at 24 px + 3 epochs at 32 px (was 4 + 4), still 8.0 total. Keep the E006 operator (flip + translate-2 at 32 px, antialiased bilinear downsample), AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1), eager Muon, and LR/EMA/lookahead rescaled to the step count, which does not change. The compiled shapes are already warmed up in build.

Explore sub-24 px phases on the E021 tip. Change only the schedule: 2 epochs at 16 px + 2 at 24 px + 4 at 32 px (8.0 total; the first two 24 px epochs become 16 px). Make the 16 px batches with the same operator (flip + translate-2 at 32 px, then antialiased bilinear to 16 px). The maps become 15/7/3/1, and AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) handles that. Compile and warm up the 16 px train shape in build. Before the scored run, measure the compiled 16 px and 20 px epoch costs with an untimed side script (2 epochs each) and log them next to the existing cost table.

Rebased I026. On the E021 tip, change only the Muon momentum from 0.6 to 0.85 (Nesterov kept, lr 0.24 unchanged). The 0.6/0.24 values come from CIFAR-10 airbench94 at bs 2000. At bs 1024 each step averages half as many examples, which usually favors higher momentum. Leave the SGD groups, schedule and resolution split unchanged.

Margin check on the current tip, with no recipe change. Using an untimed side script, run the E021 submission through the benchmark's own trial code (import it, do not edit benchmark/) on extra seeds 3-10, and record per-seed accuracy and time. The scored run is unchanged (just repeat E021) so the loop has a row, or skip scoring if the harness allows. This gauges whether the 3-seed 0.7578 reflects the 40-seed mean before margin is spent on cuts (the tip's seed 2 was 0.7523).

On the E026 tip (commit da18628: compiled batched Muon, 2@16 + 2@24 + 4@32 px, 8.0 epochs), change only the schedule to 3@16 + 1@24 + 4@32 px, so epoch 2 moves from 24 px to 16 px. Keep the same operator (flip + translate-2 at 32 px, then antialiased bilinear downsample), AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1), and Muon/SGD hyperparameters. The step count is unchanged, so the LR/EMA/lookahead schedules are unchanged too. All shapes are already warmed up in build.

On the E026 tip, change only the Muon momentum from 0.6 to 0.5 (Nesterov kept, lr 0.24, compiled update unchanged; pass momentum so nothing recompiles, or rewarm in build). E027 showed 0.85 costs 1.18 pp. This tests the other direction, since the lookahead-EMA and Nesterov already smooth the iterates and the 0.6 value was tuned on CIFAR-10 at bs 2000 without lookahead.

On the E026 tip, change only the number of Newton-Schulz iterations in the compiled batched Muon update, from 3 to 2 (same quintic coefficients, bf16). Re-warm the compiled update in build for every filter shape. Everything else is identical. The remaining Muon overhead is ~1 ms/step x 384 steps (~0.4 s, ~7% of the run), and the NS matmuls are most of it; per the E019 micro-benchmark, eager GPU time fell 3.8 -> 2.8 ms with 2 steps.

Explore the limit of the very-low-res early phase. On the E026 tip, change only the schedule to 4@16 + 4@32 px (8.0 epochs, no 24 px phase). Same operator, same Muon/SGD hyperparameters, same step count and schedules. 16 px and 32 px shapes are already warmed up in build. This is the aggressive end of the line, beyond the 3@16 + 1@24 variant, and tests whether a 24 px bridge is needed at all.

On the E026 tip (commit da18628: compiled batched Muon, 2@16 + 2@24 + 4@32 px, 8.0 epochs), change only the Newton-Schulz iteration count in the compiled Muon update from 3 to 4. Keep the quintic coefficients (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315), bf16, batching and everything else. Re-warm the compiled update in build for every filter shape. E031 showed the opposite direction (3 -> 2) costs 1.82 pp for -2.3% time. So orthogonalization quality is an accuracy knob, and one more iteration may buy margin at ~0.32 ms/step. Log per-seed accuracy and per-trial train time.

On the E026 tip, change only the Muon learning rate from 0.24 to 0.20 (momentum 0.6, Nesterov, same schedule shape; the LR is already a 0-d GPU tensor, so nothing recompiles). Both independently tuned public Muon recipes use 0.205-0.2255. E030 showed momentum is flat between 0.5 and 0.6, so lr is the one Muon knob left untested (the dropped I039 never ran).

On the E026 tip, change only how often the Muon-managed conv filters are renormalized: every 2 + int(15*progress) steps instead of every step (hiverge/Fable style). Do it inside the compiled update with a 0-d bool/int tensor flag (torch.where-gated, or two warmed-up variants selected on the host) so nothing recompiles in timed code. Warm up both paths in build. Everything else is unchanged. Before scoring, log per-step update time with CUDA events in an untimed run, to separate the renorm cost from NS.

Determinism probe on the E026 tip, with no change to the math or hyperparameters. Compile the Muon update with mode='default' instead of 'max-autotune-no-cudagraphs', and set torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark=False with cudnn.deterministic=True for all train/eval shapes. Keep the net's own compile as is. Warm everything up in build. Run the scored evaluation, then rerun seed 0 once in an untimed side script through the benchmark's trial code and compare per-seed accuracy bit for bit.

On the E026 tip, change only label smoothing from 0.3 to 0.2. Change nothing else. LS 0.3 was tuned under SGD (E009). Muon fits faster, and tuned public Muon recipes use much lower LS (0.09), so the Muon tip may be over-regularized.

On the E026 tip, raise the batch size from 1024 to 1536 (2@16 + 2@24 + 4@32 px, still 8.0 epochs). Scale the SGD param groups (BN/bias/head) by the E010 kilostep rule. Keep Muon lr 0.24 and momentum 0.6. Rescale the LR warmup/decay, EMA and lookahead schedules to the new step count (~256 steps). Compile and warm up the 1536-batch shapes at 16/24/32 px in build. The remaining Muon cost is per step (~1 ms), so a third fewer steps cuts it directly. E022 showed Muon tolerates large batches (-0.25 pp at bs 2000).
confirm rerun of E038 tip (bs 1536), H4 rule

On the E035 tip (compiled batched Muon with renorm every 2+int(15*progress) steps, 2@16 + 2@24 + 4@32 px, 8.0 epochs), change only the schedule to 3@16 + 1@24 + 4@32 px, so epoch 2 moves from 24 px to 16 px. This is E029's schedule moved onto the newer base. Use the same operator (flip + translate-2 at 32 px, then antialiased bilinear downsample) and AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1). The step count is unchanged, so the LR/EMA/lookahead/renorm schedules are unchanged. All shapes are already warmed up in build. This combines two near-misses: E029 (-0.27 s for -0.31 pp, infeasible by 0.0007) and E035's possible +0.18 pp. It does not rerun E029 unchanged (H4.2).

On the E035 tip, change only the two 24 px epochs (epochs 2-3) to 20 px: 2@16 + 2@20 + 4@32, 8.0 epochs. Use the same operator (flip + translate-2 at 32 px, antialiased bilinear to 20 px). The maps become 19/9/4/2, and AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) handles that. Compile and warm up the 20 px train shape in build. Step count and schedules are unchanged. This is an intermediate point between the 24 px bridge, which E032 showed matters (-0.68 pp without it), and a third 16 px epoch (E029, -0.31 pp). The goal is a bridge that costs ~0.40-0.45x instead of 0.57x. Log the compiled per-epoch cost of the 20 px phase.

Determinism ablation on the E035 tip, isolating half (a) of E036. Compile the Muon update with mode='default' instead of 'max-autotune-no-cudagraphs'. Keep torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark=True and do NOT set cudnn.deterministic, so the net's convs keep their benchmarked algorithms. Warm everything up in build. Run the scored evaluation. Then, in an untimed side script, rerun seed 0 twice in fresh processes through the benchmark's trial code and compare per-seed accuracy bit for bit against the scored seed 0.

On the E035 tip, use bs 2048 for the low-res phases only (the 2 epochs at 16 px and the 2 at 24 px) and keep bs 1024 for the 4@32 px tail. The goal is to halve the number of fixed-cost Muon/launch steps exactly where they are the largest share of epoch time: 16 px epochs are ~0.27 s with ~49 steps at ~1 ms of Muon each. Drive the LR/EMA/lookahead/renorm schedules by samples seen (progress = examples/total), not by step index. For the bs 2048 steps, scale the SGD groups (BN/bias/head) by the E010 kilostep rule and keep Muon lr 0.24 and momentum 0.6 (E022: Muon tolerates bs 2000). Compile and warm up the 2048-batch 16/24 px shapes in build. Run this independently of the global bs 1536 idea, since it targets the phase-local overhead.

Explore a new accuracy source. On the E035 tip, move the classifier head (the linear 576->100 after the global max pool) from SGD to the compiled Muon update. Treat its weight as a [100, 576] matrix and use Muon lr scaled by sqrt(max(1, out/in)) as for the filters, with the same momentum and 3 NS steps. Leave the head's renorm/scale handling as in the SGD version and keep the bias on SGD. Add the shape to the compiled update and warm it up in build. CIFAR-100's 100-way head is a much larger share of the learning problem than CIFAR-10's 10-way head, and public Muon recipes tuned on CIFAR-10 never tried it.

Observational, on the E026 tip with no recipe change (replacing the stale I033, which assumed eager Muon on E021). During one scored run, sample board power and SM clock via NVML at >=10 Hz in a separate monitoring process launched outside the submission (no sleeps in submission code). Tag samples by phase (16 px, 24 px, 32 px) using logged CUDA-event timestamps. Report, per phase, the fraction of time at >=95% of the 400 W cap and the mean SM clock.

On the E044 tip (bs 1536, compiled batched Muon on the 9 group convs plus the 576->100 head, renorm every 2+int(15*progress) steps, 2@16 + 2@24 + 4@32 px, 8.0 epochs), change only the schedule to 3@16 + 1@24 + 4@32 px, so epoch 2 moves from 24 px to 16 px. This is the E029/E040 near-miss moved onto the base that has margin. Keep the operator the same: flip + translate-2 at 32 px, then antialiased bilinear downsample, with AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1). The step count is unchanged, so LR, EMA, lookahead and renorm are unchanged. The 1536-batch 16 px shape is already warmed up in build. New tip only under the H4 rule.

On the E044 tip, cut half of the 24 px phase using a step-indexed switch: 2@16 + 1.5@24 + 4@32 px, 7.5 total epochs. Rescale the LR warmup/decay, EMA, lookahead and renorm schedules to the new total step count, the same way the recipe already does for epoch changes. Change nothing else, and use only shapes that are already warmed up. This tests whether a fractional removal of a cheap mid-resolution epoch, which also removes Muon steps, trades better than swapping 24 px for 16 px.

Margin check on the E044 tip (head on Muon), with no recipe change. For the scored row, rerun E044 unchanged; this is the second variance sample on the current tip. In an untimed side script, import the arena submission and run it through the benchmark's own trial code (do not edit benchmark/) on seeds 3-10. Record per-seed accuracy and time. This calibrates whether E044's +0.32 pp is real before it gets spent on schedule cuts.

On the E044 tip, change only the Muon learning rate of the classifier head group (the [100, 576] weight added in E044) from 0.24x to 0.5x of the filter Muon LR, i.e. 0.12 peak on the same schedule shape. Pass it as a separate 0-d GPU tensor so nothing recompiles. Keep the conv-filter Muon LR, momentum, NS steps and the head bias on SGD unchanged. The head's spectral-norm step size was copied from the conv filters untuned. Output layers usually want smaller normalized updates (muP-style), and the head has no renorm or wd to bound it.

On the E044 tip, narrow group 2 from 384 to 352 channels, which also shrinks group 3's first conv input. Muon handles the new filter shapes (re-batch the same-shape stacks). Recompile and warm up every train/eval shape and the Muon update in build. Change nothing else. This lever cuts FLOPs, so it should transfer to the 300 W PCIe judge better than per-step levers. Under SGD, 384->320 cost 0.115 pp per 1% (E017). Muon halved the epoch slope, so it may now trade at <=0.06 pp per 1%.

On the E044 tip, change only the LR warmup length, halving it in steps for both the SGD and Muon groups, with the same peak and the same decay end point. Everything else is unchanged. With bs 1536 the run has only ~256 steps, and the warmup was rescaled from a schedule tuned for ~408 SGD steps. Muon's normalized updates need less warmup than high-LR SGD.

Observational, on the E044 tip, with no recipe change in the scored path. In an untimed side script (same build, one trial, seed 0), wrap each phase (16/24/32 px) with CUDA events. Using torch.profiler on ~20 steps per phase, split per-step time into data augmentation (flip + translate at 32 px + antialiased downsample), net fwd/bwd, SGD foreach step, compiled Muon update, lookahead/EMA, and GPU-idle gaps. Report wall time vs GPU-busy time per phase. For the scored row, rerun E044 unchanged; it doubles as a variance sample. This gates CUDA graphs (H2.12.1) and a low-res pre-downsampled data path.

On the E046 tip (bs 1536, 3@16 + 1@24 + 4@32 px, compiled Muon on 9 convs plus head), set torch._dynamo.config.automatic_dynamic_shapes=False and raise torch._dynamo.config.cache_size_limit (e.g. 64) so that each (resolution, batch) train shape (16/24/32 px at bs 1536, plus any partial last-batch shapes) compiles as its own static graph. Warm all of them up in build on synthetic data. Keep eval on a separate compiled function that is dynamic in the batch dimension (torch._dynamo.mark_dynamic on dim 0, or the existing eval path unchanged), so any B from 1 to 1024 never recompiles. In an untimed side check, verify eval for B in {1, 7, 1000, 1024} returns finite [B,100] logits in under 5 s with no recompile. Change no math, hyperparameters or schedule. Log per-phase epoch times.

On the static-shape tip (or on E046 if H2.14.1 fails), trim a quarter of the remaining 24 px bridge with a step-indexed switch: 3@16 + 0.75@24 + 4@32 px (7.75 epochs). Rescale the LR warmup/decay, EMA, lookahead and renorm schedules to the new total step count, exactly as E047 did. Change nothing else, and use only shapes already warmed up in build. This trim is half the size of H2.10.2's arm A on purpose: at ~0.03 pp per 1%, the ~0.15 pp margin only covers a ~2-3% trim, while arm A (-0.26 s) would be expected to land at ~0.7532, right on the gate.

On the static-shape tip (or on E046 if that fails), replace AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) with x.flatten(2).amax(dim=2), which is mathematically identical (Fable: it avoids slow atomic kernels). Recompile and warm up every train and eval shape in build. Change nothing else.

On the static-shape tip (or on E046 if that fails), replace AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) with x.flatten(2).amax(dim=2), which is mathematically identical (Fable: it avoids slow atomic kernels). Recompile and warm up every train and eval shape in build. Change nothing else.

On the E046 tip (or on the static-shape tip if it is banked first), lower the LR floor of the Muon groups only (9 conv filter groups plus the head) from 0.07x to 0.05x of peak. Keep the SGD groups' floor, the warmup, the peak LR and the EMA/lookahead unchanged. Pass the value as the existing 0-d tensor schedule so nothing recompiles.
confirm rerun of E057 (H4 rule)

On the E046 tip, double the LR warmup length (0.23 -> 0.46 of the warmup fraction in steps) for both the SGD and Muon groups, keeping the same peak and the same decay end point. Change nothing else. This is the untested direction after E051, where halving the warmup cost ~0.2 pp.

On the E044 tip, cut only fixed timed overhead in prepare. Vectorize the dirac init over all 3x3 convs, and do the uint8->normalized conversion in one fused fp16 GPU op. Keep the whitening statistics on the same 5000 images, so the learned function is unchanged apart from numerics. Make sure all lazy CUDA/cuBLAS/cuDNN handles used in prepare are already initialized in build. Log the prepare and train split per trial. E004 tried this under the SGD power cap, where hidden CPU work cost nothing. In the current 5.2 s run, prepare's ~60 ms fixed cost is ~1% of time and is not overlapped with GPU-bound training.

On the E046 tip, train the whitening-stem bias only for the first 20% of steps and freeze it after that (as in hiverge and Fable). Set its LR to 0 from step 0.2*total, either through its own 0-d LR tensor or by masking it in the SGD foreach step, so nothing recompiles. Everything else is unchanged. This tests whether the 64x-LR bias groups add late-phase noise in the ~256-step regime.

Base: E060 code, which is the E057 tip (static shapes, max(dim).values pool, Muon floor 0.05) plus E060's vectorized dirac init and fused fp16 normalization in prepare. Both prepare changes are math-neutral, so the result still belongs to the pooled family, which E060 brings to 8 runs with a mean of 0.7531. Change only the head's Muon learning rate: set it to 0.5x the filter Muon LR (0.12 peak, same schedule shape and floor) as its own 0-d GPU tensor, so nothing recompiles. Leave everything else unchanged. Score it twice. Instrumentation only: log the submission source hash and a per-seed checksum of the final weights and BN buffers (for H4.4.1).
I069 second scoring (E062 code)

Base: E060 code. Change only the schedule to E047's 2@16 + 1.5@24 + 4@32 px: 7.5 total epochs with step-indexed resolution switches, and LR warmup/decay, the Muon floor, EMA, lookahead and the renorm cadence all rescaled to the new total step count, as E047 did. All three bs-1536 static shapes are already warmed up in build. Score it twice. This is the equal-time reshuffle against the 3@16 + 1@24 swap that the current tip uses.
I071 second scoring (E064 code a1aef09)

Base: E060 code. The change is Inductor kernel tuning only, aimed at the fused BN/GELU/elementwise Triton kernels, which take about 30% of GPU time (E052). Set torch._inductor.config.coordinate_descent_tuning=True and torch._inductor.config.max_autotune_pointwise=True (the net already compiles with max-autotune) before compiling the net, then recompile and warm up every static train shape plus the eval path in build. Log build time; it must stay under 600 s, and if tuning would exceed that, drop max_autotune_pointwise first. The math is unchanged apart from reduction order. Smoke-test that the loss stays finite for 10 steps before scoring.

Observational. Run an untimed side script on the E060 code with the same build and one trial on seed 0. Use torch.profiler for about 20 steps of the 32 px phase at bs 1536, and also for 20 steps at 24 px.
